summary: Reviewed all 12 supplied evidence files for the selected operator cumulative_trapezoid (candidate sha256 36033f48...c3be2703 = round-3 `.best_kernel.py`). The candidate is a faithful Triton re-implementation of torch.cumulative_trapezoid: signature `run(y, *, dx=1, dim=-1)` matches definition.json (y positional_or_keyword; dx, dim keyword-only defaults 1/-1), it allocates a fresh output (`torch.empty`, .best_kernel.py:133) so `effects.mutates=[]` / `returns_alias_of={}` hold, it does not mutate or alias `y`, it does not call torch.ops or any ATen fallback, and it has no shape/dtype/value special-casing — only the general thresholds `BLOCK > 2048` and `element_size() <= 2` (.best_kernel.py:143-152). The oracle (oracle.py:71-80) is the independent `torch.cumulative_trapezoid` reference and does not import or register the candidate, so the reference is not circular; `gen_inputs` builds inputs from the spec including the transposed (non-contiguous) variants. Optimization rounds 1-3 measured 33/33 workloads passing each round (`.ledger.json`:49, 527, 1402), the final retest re-verified 33/33 at geo_mean 0.5217 (optimize_definition_output.json:8-12), and the harness preflight/evaluate records PASSED with reference-vs-reference ratios ~1.0 and identical outputs (preflight.json:2-9, evaluate.json:3-18). No evidence of reward hacking (`is_hack=false` in every ledger round and in preflight/evaluate). Remaining issues are advisory: fp64 is advertised but accumulated in fp32, the large-N strided path has no tiling guard, some candidate branches are not exercised by any correctness case, and the delivered kernel is still ~1.9x slower than the reference in aggregate. Note: `review_tests/attempts/01/review.json` records an explicit skip for a *different* subject sha256 (30820d94...) and was not treated as acceptance of this candidate. No source index / pinned FlagGems source was supplied for this kind, so the comparison baseline used is the frozen evaluation contract plus the ledger's round-1 seed.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:111-116 asserts support for torch.float64 (`assert y.dtype in (float16, bfloat16, float32, float64)`), but every compute path narrows to fp32 before accumulating: .best_kernel.py:39-42 (`tl.load(...).to(tl.float32)`, `s = (a + b) * SCALE`, `tl.cumsum`), .best_kernel.py:73-75 (long-row tiles), .best_kernel.py:101-104 (strided path). The reference preserves fp64: oracle.py:79-80 returns `torch.cumulative_trapezoid(**kwargs)`. No fp64 case exists in the contract (correctness.jsonl:17-24 stops at float32; timing.jsonl:7-9 likewise), so 33/33 PASS cannot detect this. The same `.to(tl.float32)` appears in the round-1 seed (.ledger.json:34), so this is inherited rather than newly introduced, but the delivered function still claims and returns fp64 results at fp32 precision.
findings.reason: For a float64 input the candidate silently computes the running sum in float32 (~7 decimal digits) and casts back to fp64, so the returned values are not the fp64 reference result; e.g. a long row accumulates an error orders of magnitude above what an fp64 caller would tolerate, while the function explicitly advertises that dtype. Because no workload uses fp64, the correctness gate cannot catch it, and the failure would surface only in downstream use.
findings.requested_change: Either dispatch on `y.dtype` and accumulate in `tl.float64` (including an fp64 `SCALE`) when `y.dtype is torch.float64`, or remove torch.float64 from the supported-dtype assert and from the advertised dtype set so the unsupported case fails loudly instead of returning silently degraded values. If fp64 accumulation is not feasible on the target, keep the explicit rejection and record it as a target-capability limit.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:143 sets `BLOCK = triton.next_power_of_2(max(N - 1, 1))` and the `inner != 1` branch (.best_kernel.py:155-158) launches one program per column with that whole BLOCK and a single `tl.cumsum`, i.e. there is no N-tiling/carry for the strided path. The `inner == 1` long path instead uses a compile-time-unrolled loop: `NCH: tl.constexpr` with `for n in range(NCH)` (.best_kernel.py:54, 70) over 3D triangular broadcasts of shape (C,B,B) (.best_kernel.py:65-81), with C chosen by element size (.best_kernel.py:146-152). UB pressure on this backend is already demonstrated: `.ledger.json`:2221 records the preflight failure 'requires 1708800 bits while 1572864 bits available' for the C=64,B=16 fp32 tile, and `.ledger.json`:1365 documents the resulting forced narrowing to C=16 for 4-byte elements.
findings.reason: Both branches scale compile-time resources with the scan length instead of streaming over it: for `inner != 1` any N above ~2049 compiles a single-program cumsum over next_power_of_2(N-1) elements (e.g. a [4096,128] dim=0 input), and for contiguous rows the unrolled `NCH` loop plus (C,B,B) reduction tensors multiply per-N work at compile time. Given that a 64x16 fp32 tile already exceeded the 192 KiB UB, larger N is at real risk of compile failure or UB overflow. None of the 9 timing shapes probes this (the three dim=0 cases are 1024x128, N=1024 -> BLOCK=1024, `.best_kernel.py`:143).
findings.requested_change: Tile the strided scan over N with an fp32 carry (reusing the long-row scheme) instead of one full-length cumsum per column, and make the long-row chunk count a runtime loop bound (or cap NCH) so compiled code does not grow with N. Add a large-N `inner != 1` probe (e.g. N=4097 with dim=0) to the evidence before claiming general shape support.

findings.evidence: The 24 correctness cases only use scan lengths N in {2..17}: shape [3,17], [7,9], [3,1] (correctness.jsonl:1-24), so `BLOCK` is at most 16 and the `BLOCK > 2048` long-row branch (.best_kernel.py:146-152) is never correctness-checked by a dedicated case; it is exercised only by the timing workloads 1024x4096 dx=1 at fp16/bf16/fp32 (timing.jsonl:2, 5, 8) and only at dx=1, so the folded `SCALE` path (.best_kernel.py:139) is not covered for long rows. The `inner != 1` strided path with N-1 > 2048 is executed by no workload at all: the three dim=0 timing cases are 1024x128 (timing.jsonl:3, 6, 9), i.e. N=1024 -> BLOCK=1024, which goes to `_cumtrapz_strided_kernel` (good) but with the small-BLOCK configuration. fp64 is never exercised (correctness.jsonl:1-24, timing.jsonl:1-9).
findings.reason: The two riskiest paths (large-BLOCK strided scan; long-row scan with dx != 1) and the advertised fp64 dtype have no direct correctness case, so a defect localized to them would not be attributed by the gate even though the evaluator does compare timing workloads numerically. This is a coverage limitation of the frozen workload list, not a candidate defect.
findings.requested_change: Add correctness workloads such as a dim=0 case with a long scan axis (e.g. [4096,128] float16/float32), a long-row case with dx != 1 (e.g. [4,4097] dx=0.25), and one float64 case (e.g. [3,17] float64 with an fp64-appropriate tolerance). Keep these as catalog coverage additions rather than changes to the candidate.

findings.evidence: Final verification reports geo_mean 0.5217, and every individual ratio in `.ledger.json`:1697-1803 is <= 0.591 except timing-5 (1.878); worst case timing-7 (float32 1024x4096) is 0.316 (0.998 ms vs 0.316 ms reference, `.ledger.json`:1781-1790), and the dim=0 strided cases are 0.160 ms vs 0.054-0.059 ms (timing-2/8, `.ledger.json`:1720-1730, 1792-1802). The round-3 profile and conclusion attribute the residual gap to the tl.cumsum lowering and to the UB-capped fp32 long-row tile (`.ledger.json`:2215, 2221-2222), and the non-contiguous correctness inputs additionally pay a full `y.contiguous()` copy (.best_kernel.py:141).
findings.reason: Optimize status PASSED reflects the correctness/regression gate only; the delivered kernel is still ~1.9x slower than the torch reference in aggregate (geo_mean 0.52 < 1) and ~3x slower on the two dominant families, so the performance objective of this run is not met by the current artifact. This is a residual optimization gap, not a contract violation, and no code change is required to accept correctness.
findings.requested_change: No blocking change. Carry the residual gaps forward as optimization work: a 2D (T, inner) column-tile scan with a vector carry for the dim!=last strided cases, a wider C for the 4-byte long-row tile within the UB budget, and avoidance of the full contiguous copy for transposed inputs where the stride is compile-time known.
